items.title: Replace or redesign deterministic-token cryptography
items.short_title: Replace or redesign deterministic-token cryptography

note_records.text: **2026-10-07** — Decisions (owner-approved 2026-10-07): Algorithm = AES-SIV-CMAC-256 (RFC 5297; two AES-128 keys), implemented in-repo in Obfuscator/AesSiv.cs on BCL Aes.EncryptEcb; a .NET 10.0.12 probe found no public CMAC/SIV type in the BCL. No new dependency. Token = OBF_TK2_ + base64url(SIV||CTR ciphertext) over UTF-8 + PKCS7 padding to 16 bytes (length leak unchanged from CBC). Per-column key = HKDF(master, '<column>|token-siv', 32); AD = column name. Joinability scope unchanged: per column, per manifest salt. Compatibility: manifest Version 2.1, ColumnObfuscationSpec.TokenScheme='aes-siv-cmac-256/v1' (omitted when null so 2.0 checksums verify); TokenScheme null => legacy OBF_TKN_ CBC decrypt-only path, CBC encrypt removed. Unknown scheme throws. Public API signatures unchanged.

**2026-10-07** — Ready for review: branch ob-04-aes-siv-tokens (c3c83a6 claim, 8bd80f3 implementation). Behaviour change: new deterministic tokens are AES-SIV OBF_TK2_; tampered or wrong-key tokens now throw InvalidOperationException without echoing values; old OBF_TKN_ manifests still deobfuscate. Checks: RFC 4493 CMAC vectors (4) and RFC 5297 A.1/A.2 pass; tamper/AD/truncation, equality/distinct/cross-column, prefix-leak regression, 15/16/17-byte + UTF-8 round-trip and length buckets, wrong key, legacy golden fixture (generated by main @ fc19ca7) pass; dotnet test Obfuscator.slnx 91/91 passed; scripts/test-local.sh exit 0, token columns restore exactly. macOS only locally; Linux/Windows left to CI. Round-trip tests are not a security argument: correctness rests on the RFC KATs and the construction still needs reviewer sign-off. Follow-up filed: ob-13 (float columns do not round-trip exactly; pre-existing).

**2026-10-08** — VERDICT: PASS. Reviewed AesSiv.cs line-by-line against RFC 4493 (subkeys, CMAC last-block handling) and RFC 5297 (S2V incl. xorend/pad branches, Q bit-31/63 clearing, 128-bit counter, constant-time tag compare, plaintext zeroed on failure); KATs RFC 4493 x4, RFC 5297 A.1/A.2 pass. Engine: per-column HKDF key with distinct info label, AD = column name, cache reset on each BindCrypto; no derivation collision with mapping mode (string mode is global per run). Compat: 2.0 manifests verify and decrypt via legacy path (golden fixture); older builds reject 2.1 token manifests via checksum mismatch rather than passing tokens through. Checks: dotnet test 91/91, scripts/test-local.sh exit 0, slicer check pass (macOS). Non-blocking: Version field is never validated on read; token AesSiv instances are not disposed after the final run.

items.title: Floating-point columns do not round-trip exactly
items.short_title: Floating-point columns do not round-trip exactly

note_records.text: **2026-10-08** — Ready for review: branch ob-13-exact-floats (f40d59c claim, a9b3b5d implementation). Behaviour change: new manifests (version 2.2) transform floating columns with exact decimal arithmetic (new internal ExactDecimal, BigInteger mantissa x 10^exponent); specs record FloatScheme exact-decimal/v1, ExactScale (4 decimals) and ExactShift (4 significant digits), omitted when null so pre-2.2 checksums verify; pre-2.2 manifests keep the double path. Restores the same numeric value, not always the same text (5.0 -> 5, 1,000.5 -> 1000.5). Cells beyond 1000 significant digits or |exponent| ~1100 take the string path and count as unparsed (--strict rejects). Edited float cells fail without echoing the value. README documents exactness, normalization, and that exact output reveals roughly how many decimal places the original had. Checks: regression FloatingColumn_RoundTripsToSameNumericValue failed on main (131.60538314346292 -> 131.6053831434628) and passes; round-trip theory over 215 values x 6 transforms (incl. 5e-324, 1e300, -MaxValue, infinite shift), ExactDecimal parse/format/reject, tamper, unknown scheme, legacy spec, unbounded-cell tests pass; dotnet test Obfuscator.slnx 177/177; scripts/test-local.sh exit 0 with new assert_restored (cells byte-equal or numerically equal; plain cmp failed only on -40.0/5.0 normalization); slicer check passed. macOS only locally. No follow-ups filed.

**2026-10-08** — VERDICT: FAIL - obfuscate bounds only the input cell, not the output: a cell within ExactDecimal limits (e.g. 1e-1000 against shift ~1e3, or a 1000-digit value) produces y with more than 1000 significant digits, which deobfuscate cannot parse, so it falls through to the string path and the obfuscated value is written back as the 'restored' value with no error. Reproduced with a CSV round-trip test (restored cell is the obfuscated value).

**2026-10-08** — Ready for review: branch ob-13-exact-floats, fix commit 124024d after review failure 10e2d22. Change: new TryObfuscateExactFloat transforms a cell only when its output also parses within ExactDecimal bounds, and is the unparsed test for floating columns (ParsesAsKind now takes the spec), so such cells are mapped/tokenized and counted like other non-numeric values instead of being written back unchanged on deobfuscate. README bound sentence now covers the transformed value. Checks: new FloatingColumn_CellWhoseOutputExceedsParseBounds_RoundTrips (1e-1000 and a 1000-digit value) failed before the fix (restored cell was the obfuscated value) and passes, with UnparsedValueCounts 2; dotnet test Obfuscator.slnx 178/178; scripts/test-local.sh exit 0 with assert_restored; slicer check passed.

**2026-10-30** — Owner answer (generate.preamble-counter): option c. A preamble counter entry prints its start value only; step is kept in the config for future appended blocks.

**2026-10-30** — Owner fix note: in-limit values must not be clamped onto the limits (golden shows values exactly at upper/lower limit). Redraw a value that falls outside its limits instead of clamping; out-of-limit values are still produced only at outOfLimitRate. Rebaseline the golden.

**2026-10-30** — Owner fix note: the example config and golden must not inject stray bytes; that corruption is a bug in the real sources, not something fake data should carry. Keep preamble.inject as an opt-in option (off by default) with its tests, remove it from ExampleConfigTestResults.json, rebaseline the golden as clean UTF-8, and document inject as off by default. **2026-10-30** — The example config and golden carry no injected bytes, the golden is clean UTF-8 with CRLF, inject is opt-in and off by default and still covered by inline tests, the limit check stays inclusive on the printed value per the owner; 304 tests green, build/format/test-local pass.

goals: Make CSV obfuscation and restoration safer to use for library and CLI users, while maintaining synthetic CSV generation as an equally important product capability. Harden the current 0.1 line over the next 1–2 releases, prioritizing safe data handling and risk reduction.
non_goals: Do not claim obfuscation alone provides cryptographic secrecy. Do not require encrypted manifests by default. Do not target a 1.0 release in this roadmap.
